I've been farming these 16.1 mu for 40 years now. Me and my wife, we're the only two left in the household — the children went to the city long ago. I'm 67, my back isn't what it used to be, but I still know every inch of this land. I only finished primary school, so I don't read those extension pamphlets much. I watch what my neighbors do and I remember what happened on my own fields.

**Wheat (10 mu):** I planted the wheat last October, same as always. The stand looks decent this spring. Before planting I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's my base. Now it's March, the wheat is greening up. I'll irrigate once when the weather warms, and at jointing I'll spread another half-bag of urea per mu. If the leaves look yellow, maybe a bit more. My neighbor Lao Zhang uses more fertilizer and sometimes gets 500 kg per mu, but I can't afford to risk that much money on inputs. I use about 18 kg of nitrogen total per mu, and I expect around 420 kg per mu if the weather holds. I'll irrigate three times total counting the winter irrigation I already did. The wild oats are bad this year, so I'll spray herbicide once in spring. Come early June, I'll hire three or four people for a couple days to help with harvest — me and my wife can't cut and thresh it alone anymore.

**Maize (10 mu, same land after wheat):** This is always the hard part — maybe one week between wheat harvest and maize planting. I hire a fellow with a tractor to rotavate quick, then I plant by hand or sometimes rent the planter. I use hybrid seed, about 3-4 kg per mu, costs me around 60 yuan. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, maybe 15 kg worth per mu, and then at the big trumpet stage I topdress with urea if the rains haven't been good. Total nitrogen about 16 kg per mu. I irrigate twice if the summer rains are normal, three times if it's dry like two years ago. Last year I got 460 kg per mu, so I'll hope for that again. I hire extra hands for planting and harvest because the window is so tight.

**Stevia (6.1 mu):** I started this three years back because a buyer from the county said he'd purchase the dried leaves. It's not like grain — you pick the leaves, not the whole plant. Less heavy work, but you have to tend it through the summer. I fertilize it lighter than grain, about 10 kg nitrogen per mu, split twice — once in spring and once after the first leaf picking. I irrigate twice, maybe three times if it's very hot. I don't spray much pesticide on it, just pull the weeds by hand. I expect about 200 kg of dry leaves per mu. The price is decent but not as steady as grain, so I don't rely on it too much.

**Labor and money:** Me and my wife do most of the work ourselves — about 65 family days across all three crops. But for wheat harvest, maize planting, and maize harvest, I have to hire about 15 days of labor at 150 yuan a day now. Seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, pumping water, and hired labor all together cost me about 6,200 yuan this year. That's a lot of money when there's only two of us and we're on pension age. I keep some cash aside for medicine and emergencies. That's why I don't push fertilizer to the maximum — yes, more might give more yield, but what if prices drop or the drought hits? Better to be a little safe. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps, so I do what I did last year unless I have a strong reason to change.
